description: Turn Claude Code into a full game dev studio — 49 AI agents, 72 workflow skills, and a complete coordination system mirroring real studio hierarchy.

summary.one_liner: A template that turns a Claude Code session into a simulated game development studio, with 49 role-based AI agents, 74 slash-command skills, hooks, and coding rules for Godot, Unity, or Unreal projects.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a project template containing agent definitions organized in a three-tier studio hierarchy (directors, department leads, specialists), with per-engine agent sets for Godot 4, Unity, and Unreal Engine 5. It ships 74 slash-command skills covering the production pipeline from brainstorming and game design docs through architecture, epics and stories, sprints, reviews, QA, and release. Fifteen hooks run validation on git commits and pushes, design doc reads and writes, asset JSON, and agent audit logging. Fourteen path-scoped rules enforce coding standards by directory, such as gameplay, core, AI, networking, and UI code. A project.yaml file with a modes.rigor setting (minimal, standard, or full) controls how much documentation and process the skills require. The README states that agents follow an ask-present options-draft-approve protocol and do not write without user sign-off.
use_cases: Structuring a solo indie game project with AI assistance
Generating game design documents and tracking them against code
Breaking a game design into epics, stories, and sprint plans
Running design, code, and QA review passes on game features
Setting up coding standards and validation hooks for a Godot, Unity, or Unreal project
Planning a game release with checklists and patch notes
how_to_run: claude  (start Claude Code in the project root folder that holds CLAUDE.md and project.yaml)
/setup-engine godot 4.7  (or another engine version, if you already know your engine)
stack: Markdown with YAML frontmatter (agents and skills)
Godot 4, Unity, or Unreal Engine 5 (target engine)
notable: Three-tier studio hierarchy of 49 agents, with models assigned per agent in frontmatter
modes.rigor setting (minimal, standard, full) that sets documentation and QA depth from one control
Requires a running game and a retained screenshot before a visual story counts as done
Hooks that block or warn on hardcoded values, design-doc size, registry edits, and git push to protected branches
studio-tests directory with a linter and behavioral specs for testing edited skills and agents
caveats: The games built with it are not included; it is a template to clone, not a finished game
Hooks depend on Python 3 and Bash; without Python, settings fall back to defaults and data-JSON commits are blocked
Desktop notifications are only wired for Windows; the notify hook is a no-op on macOS and Linux
Starting Claude Code in a subfolder skips project hooks and permission rules
